newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.Europe rapeseed seen firm to 1st quarter 1997.
newsitem.headline: N.Europe rapeseed seen firm to 1st quarter 1997.

text.p: Rapeseed prices in northwest Europe were seen firm until February/March 1997 in sympathy with a global oilseeds price strength, brokers said on Friday.
They pointed to good demand for soy and rape oil in Rotterdam markets and rape meal ordering from compound feed manufacturers for the winter months.
But they added dollar movements and U.S. soya harvest news were as crucial to winter season prices as local factors.

December buyers free Hamburg were unchanged from November bids last week of 460 marks a tonne, with trade buyers a few marks higher and sellers holding out for the 467.50 marks briefly paid for January earlier this week.
But physical trade volumes were slim because soybeans and sunseeds offered crushers better margins.
Rapeseed buyers at points other than Hamburg offered 445 marks for November fob Mittellandkanal, compared with a 440-455 marks national range last week.
The Dec buyer range was 442-462.50 marks after Dec traded at 451 last week cif Lower Rhine.
January buyers of French seed fob Moselle offered 1,530 francs versus 1,480 francs last week and 1,550 francs for April.
German August 1997 buyers emerged with offers at 420-430.
Protests from European consumer and environmentalist lobbies over possible risks from genetically-altered U.S. soybeans continued but failed to influence markets.
Crushers were busy with the processing of new soybean arrivals.
Local spot rape meal sellers (34 percent protein) were steady at 30.25 marks/100 kg, with Dec up 0.50 marks up at 30.00, and Jan-April 0.65 marks up on the week at 29.15.
By comparison, Nov soymeal (44 percent) was at 43.65-44.00 marks, Dec at 43.40 and Jan-April at 41.50.
Local Dec rape oil sellers were off 0.25 at 82.75 marks/100 kg, Jan oil was at 83.50 (previously unquoted) and Feb/April at 24.25 (off 0.50).
